tail:
VERDICT: CLEAN
BOUNDARY: Isolated points (A={c}) give ω_f(c)=0 and continuity vacuously; the proof handles them because ω_f({c})=0 and the δ from continuity still works. Unbounded f near c may yield ω_f(A∩N_δ(c))=+∞, but the extended‑real comparisons (e.g., +∞≥ε) and the infimum argument remain valid. No division by zero, empty index families, or degenerate intervals occur. All boundary cases are correctly covered.
SOURCES: Inspected every cited item: def-continuity-real (ε‑δ definition, neighbourhood formulation), def-oscillation (definitions of ω_f(S) and ω_f(c), nonnegativity, relationship ω_f(c)≤ω_f(A∩N_δ(c))), def-extended-reals (order on \overline{\mathbb{R}}), lem-extended-reals-complete (existence of sup/inf in \overline{\mathbb{R}} and their bounding properties), def-neighbourhood-r (N_δ(c) as open interval), lem-of-abs-value (triangle inequality). Each supplies the exact properties used.
CHECKED: Title, public statement, every numbered proof step (1.1, 1.2, 2.1, 2.2, 3.1, 4.1), and Remarks. The forward implication (continuity ⇒ ω_f(c)=0) and the converse (ω_f(c)=0 ⇒ continuity) are correctly derived from the cited definitions and the completeness of \overline{\mathbb{R}}. No logical gap or false inference was found.
